# NAB FY25 Business & Private Banking — was the growth value-accretive?

**Judgment: broadly yes, but the incremental dollar earned less.** B&PB grew volume across
sectors, did not buy 2H volume with price, and its business-lending credit charge actually
fell. What it gave up was operating leverage and capital efficiency, not underwriting
discipline.

## 1. The reconciliation (FY25 v FY24)

| Line | FY25 | Move |
|---|---|---|
| GLAs / business lending | $279.5bn / $166.3bn | +6.8% / +7.3% |
| Average interest earning assets | $249.0bn | +5.4% |
| Net interest income | $7,499m | +2.8% |
| Net operating income | $8,531m | +2.1% |
| Operating expenses | $3,232m | +2.9% |
| Credit impairment charge | $529m | +1.1% |
| Cash earnings | $3,330m | +1.6% |
| Risk-weighted assets | $159.2bn | +9.0% |

Cash earnings rose $53m: NII +$204m, other income −$31m, costs −$91m, credit −$6m, tax −$23m.
6.8% of volume became 1.6% of earnings through three leaks — NIM −8bps (3.09%→3.01%), negative
jaws (cost-to-income 37.6%→37.9%), and RWA growth outrunning GLA growth. Return on average assets
fell 5bps to 1.25%; return on **average RWA was flat at 2.18%**. The new book earned roughly the
average risk-adjusted return but consumed more capital per dollar lent.

## 2. Margin: a real cost, but not the price of 2H volume

The 8bps is attributed to competition in *both* business and housing lending *and* to higher
deposit costs and mix — deposit cost is not a price paid for loan growth. The second-half test
is decisive: GLAs +4.5% HoH while NIM rose 1bp to 3.02%, and the Group NIM bridge shows lending
margin flat with Australian business lending only −1bp. B&PB's 3.01% NIM remains 1.7x the Group's
1.74% and the highest of any division, and APRA business-lending share rose 21.5%→21.7%.

## 3. Credit: the charge exonerates, the stock warns

**P&L:** B&PB's *business lending* charge **fell** from $517m to $431m; the divisional charge rose
only because home lending swung from −$7m to +$53m. Charge/GLAs improved 1bp to 0.19%. Mix barely
moved (sub-investment-grade 78%→77%, fully secured 74%→73%, PD≥2.5% 14% at Mar-25 and Sep-25).

**Balance sheet:** B&PB NPEs rose 26.9% to $7,079m (2.12%→2.54% of GLAs) — four times lending
growth. Business-lending NPLs reached 3.22% of business GLAs (impaired 0.60%→0.73%), the highest
in the series disclosed back to Sep-16, and 2H25 charges jumped to $292m (0.21% annualised).

## 4. Broad-based versus single-name

**Growth is broad-based:** Other +10.4% ($68bn), Small business +9.2% ($13bn), CRE +7.4% ($42bn),
Health +5.9% ($10bn), Agri +3.5% ($46bn).

**Deterioration is not co-located with growth.** The Group's *impaired* step-up is single names in
C&IB and NZ Banking, not B&PB. B&PB's contribution is the default-but-not-impaired ratio — and the
2H25 move there is explicitly "a small number of large customers in the Agriculture portfolio",
narrowed elsewhere to "two large well secured customers". Australian agriculture NPE/EAD jumped
1.99%→2.95%, yet Agri was the *slowest*-growing sector (+3.5%). CRE grew 7.4% with its NPE ratio
up only 5bps YoY (and down HoH). Group watch loans fell 9bps to 1.17%, the first decline since
Mar-23. NAB describes the FY25 default-but-not-impaired rise as portfolio-wide, so the underlying
drift is broad; the visible 2H spike is lumpy, in a low-growth, well-secured book.

**Bottom line:** value-accretive in level (B&PB+C&IB combined ROE 18%), dilutive at the margin.
The binding constraint is capital and cost, not spread or underwriting.

key_facts.fact: The growth was largely self-funded by low-cost deposits: B&PB customer deposits grew 6.6% ($14.8bn) to $237.9bn, from on-demand deposits (+$10.3bn) and non-interest bearing accounts (+$5.0bn), with term deposits DOWN $0.5bn.

citations.quote: an increase of $14.8 billion or 6.6% in Business and Private Banking driven by underlying growth in on-demand deposits of $10.3 billion and non-interest bearing accounts including offsets of $5.0 billion, partially offset by a decrease in term deposits of $0.5 billion.

key_facts.fact: The only return-on-equity disclosure for the business bank is 18%, and it is for B&PB and C&IB COMBINED on a cash earnings / average RWA basis at an 11.25% CET1 ratio - well above the Group cash ROE of 11.4%.

citations.quote: Combined Business Banking 18% ROE ... FY25 ROE for B&PB and C&IB combined, based on cash earnings/average RWA and 11.25% CET1 ratio, excludes centrally held RWA and deductions
Cash return on equity 11.4% 11.6% (20 bps) 11.0% 11.7% (70 bps)

limitations: No stand-alone ROE or allocated equity is disclosed for B&PB. The only ROE shown (18%) covers B&PB and C&IB combined, on a cash earnings / average RWA basis at 11.25% CET1, excluding centrally held RWA and deductions. B&PB's own return cannot be isolated.

The 8bps B&PB NIM decline is not decomposed into lending margin, deposit margin and replicating-portfolio effects at divisional level. Only the Group bridge is split, so the exact share of margin genuinely surrendered to win business lending volume is not measurable.
No front-book versus back-book spread is disclosed for business lending. The documents therefore cannot show whether new FY25 volume was written at a lower spread than the existing book.
The B&PB credit impairment charge and non-performing exposure charts (presentation p.95) explicitly include mortgages, so the divisional ratios blend the business and housing credit cycles.

No credit impairment charge, loss rate or non-performing ratio is disclosed for the individual growth sectors. 'Other' is the largest ($68bn, ~41% of the business book) and the fastest-growing (+10.4%), yet has no separate asset quality disclosure.
The industry sector NPL chart (presentation p.87) carries no printed values, so sector-level deterioration cannot be quantified from these documents.

The agriculture asset quality data on presentation p.97 is Group Australian EAD, spanning B&PB and C&IB. The dollar amount of the B&PB Agriculture single-name downgrades is not quantified anywhere in these documents.
The PD >= 2.0% higher-risk series stops at Mar 25 and the PD >= 2.5% series starts at Mar 25 (Pillar 3 Table CR6 basis). There is no like-for-like Sep 24 to Sep 25 comparison of higher-risk balances.

FY24 comparatives are restated twice - for a lending and deposit portfolio transfer between Personal Banking and B&PB, and for a change in expense presentation. The growth rates are not against originally reported FY24 figures.
No divisional FTE or banker headcount is given, so the cost of the 'investment in additional bankers' driving the 3.2% underlying expense increase cannot be sized.

Presentation of term deposits appears inconsistent in emphasis: the B&PB NIM commentary cites 'mix impacts due to term deposit growth', while the spot balance sheet shows B&PB term deposits fell $0.5bn over FY25. This is most likely an average-balance versus spot-balance difference, but the documents do not reconcile it. I prefer the spot disclosure for the balance question and accept the NIM commentary for the average-balance margin effect.

Several figures used here (the business/housing/other split of the B&PB charge, the NPE split, security and grade mix, sector growth rates) are read from unlabelled or partially labelled presentation charts. I rendered each chart to confirm the series assignment, but the underlying values are not published in tabular form.
